newsitem.title: THAILAND: Fighting flares in northwest Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Fighting flares in northwest Cambodia.

text.p: Fighting flared between rival factions in northwest Cambodia on Sunday and many civilians were preparing to seek refuge on the Thai side of the border, a Thai army officer said.
The officer, based in northeastern Thailand near the border with Cambodia, said preparations were being made to receive an influx of refugees from Cambodia.
"We heard fighting today but we don't yet have a report about which factions are involved," the officer told Reuters.
The fighting was in the area of Samrong town which had been held by royalist forces loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Government officials in Phnom Penh said on Saturday that forces under Second Prime Minister Hun Sen had taken over part of Samrong on Friday and talks were under way with the royalist commanders there.
A senior military officer in Phnom Penh denied that any fighting was going on.
"It's quiet. The area is totally under the control of the government," General Mol Reup told Reuters. Mol Reup also denied that negotiations were under way with royalist forces in the area.

The Thai officer said Cambodian civilians were preparing to seek refuge in Thailand and local authorities had designated an area for them. The refugees would be allowed to cross the border when the situation became serious, he said.
"There are a number of Cambodian people near the border crossing point but I cannot estimate how many people in all," the officer said.
"For the time being they are safe, the fighting is deep inside Cambodia near Samrong," he said. Samrong is about 30 km (20 miles) from the border.
Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh on July 6 after two days of fighting in the capital. Their forces in northern Cambodia began fighting soon after and royalist troops were quickly pushed back towards Samrong.

On Saturday Hun Sen rejected efforts by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to find a peaceful solution to Cambodia's current crisis. Ranariddh told reporters in Bangkok Hun Sen's stance would mean more war.
